    """Hash `raw` into a storable credential value."""

comments.content: chunkIdentities mints a brand-new SegmentStorage (and thus a new global identity token) for every chunk on every read. Sequence `write(x); flush()` while `!isLive` leaves `x` in `buffered` because `flush()` early-returns, and the later `activate()` only flips `isLive` without flushing.     global _DROPPED_FAILURES

comments.content: Naive bracket scan ignores strings/comments/char classes: counting every `(`/`)` or `{`/`}` means a `")"`, `"}"`, `// )` or `/* } */` inside the span prematurely closes `_balanced_content` (truncated `allSatisfy`/`for` bodies, truncated param lists) or over-merges to a later bracket. The silent fallback `return text[open_idx+1:]` on unbalanced input then scans the rest of the file. Skip Swift strings (`"..."`, triple-quoted), line/block comments, and handle escapes when counting depth; return `""` or signal failure on unbalanced instead of the tail.
comments.suggestion_code:
def _balanced_content(text: str, open_idx: int, open_char: str = "(", close_char: str = ")") -> str:
    """Text strictly between the bracket at `open_idx` and its match."""
    depth = 0
    i = open_idx
    n = len(text)
    state = None  # None | 'line_comment' | 'block_comment' | '"' | '...'
    while i < n:
        # TODO: skip //, /* */, "...", \"\"\"...\"\"\" with escapes before depth counting
        c = text[i]
        if c == open_char:
            depth += 1
        elif c == close_char:
            depth -= 1
            if depth == 0:
                return text[open_idx + 1 : i]
        i += 1
    return ""

String-literal parens are routine in Swift, so allSatisfy/for bodies and param lists truncate or over-merge, matching the confirmed batch-02 #745 lexical-detector class.

comments.content: Tee-pump exceptions are swallowed and the partial digest is recorded as authoritative. Capture the thread exception and degrade to `unavailable`/exit 3 instead of recording.

comments.content: Treating `#...` as a line comment corrupts Swift brace tracking (and `//...` corrupts Python `//` floor-division). In Swift `if #available(...) {` / `#if ... {` the opening `{` is blanked by `_mask()` while its closer stays visible, so the brace counter closes early and the body is truncated. Conversely in Python `x = a // b` the `// b` tail is dropped as a comment, polluting fingerprints. The single master regex cannot serve both language families.
comments.suggestion_code:
| (?P<CPP_COMMENT//[^\n]*)  # Swift/Kotlin only — do not apply to Python
    | (?P<PY_COMMENT\#[^\n]*)  # Python only — do not apply to Swift/Kotlin
# Then _mask(text, is_python: bool) blanks only the comment kind for that language,
# and _normalize_tokens() skips only the matching kind.

validation.notes: Demonstrated live: _mask blanks `if #available(iOS 16, *) {`'s brace, so the Swift brace counter (:322-333) closes early and truncates bodies; and `x = a // b` tokenizes identically to `x = a` (Python floordiv eaten as comment), corrupting fingerprints toward false clones. The single language-agnostic LINE_COMMENT regex (:234) serving both extractors (:297,:346) is the certain cause; per-language comment kinds fix it.

comments.content: 13 unpruned `find .` scans (one per extension) walk `.git/.build/node_modules/vendor` every time and `| head -2000` is applied per-extension (up to ~26k counted), skewing the 200/800 corpus gates and making preflight slow on large repos. Use a single pruned find with grouped predicates and count once, e.g. `find . -path ./.git -prune -o -path ./node_modules -prune -o -type f \( -name '*Test*' ... \) -print`. Avoid the bash `while read` increment loop — `wc -l` or `mapfile` is far faster.
